title: Unit 9 · The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge
titleTranslate: 第九单元·港珠澳大桥
text:
The construction of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge started on 15 December 2009.
It cost a total of 126.9 billion yuan and took nine years to be completed.
It was put into use on 24 October 2018.
The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge connects Hong Kong on the east bank of the Pearl River Delta to Zhuhai and Macao on the west bank.
The bridge covers a distance of 55 kilometres, making it the longest sea-crossing bridge in the world.
The project has set many world records.
It provides valuable construction experience for building such sea-crossing bridges in the future.
The bridge includes a tunnel that is 6.7 kilometres long—the world's deepest underwater tunnel.

A total of more than 400,000 tons of steel were used for the tunnel and the 22.9-kilometre bridge, which is enough to build 60 Eiffel Towers.
The bridge was named one of the "seven wonders of the modern world".

The bridge was designed to withstand strong earthquakes and super typhoons.
Before the construction of the bridge, it took more than 3 hours to drive from Hong Kong to Zhuhai and Macao.
Now it takes only about 45 minutes.
It is important not only to the development of bridge building but also to the economic and social development.
The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge is a testament to the collective efforts of thousands of individuals, reflecting the wisdom, strength, and determination of the Chinese people.
textTranslate:
港珠澳大桥于2009年12月15日开工建设。
大桥总投资126.9亿元，历时九年建成。
大桥于2018年10月24日正式通车。
港珠澳大桥连接珠江三角洲东岸的香港与西岸的珠海和澳门。
大桥全长55千米，是世界上最长的跨海大桥。
该项目创造了多项世界纪录。
它为未来建造此类跨海大桥提供了宝贵的施工经验。
大桥包括一条长6.7公里的隧道，是世界上最深的水下隧道。

隧道和长22.9公里的大桥共使用40多万吨钢材，足以建造60座埃菲尔铁塔。
这座大桥被列为“世界现代七大奇迹”之一。

大桥的设计能够抵御强烈地震和超强台风。
大桥建成前，从香港驱车前往珠海和澳门需要3个多小时。
现在只需大约45分钟。
它不仅对桥梁建设的发展，而且对经济和社会的发展都具有重要意义。
港珠澳大桥是千万人共同努力的见证，凝聚了中国人民的智慧、力量和决心。

title: Unit 9 · What can be regarded as symbols of China?
titleTranslate: 第九单元 · 什么可以被视为中国的象征？
text:
Li Na's vacation was terrible.
Peter went to Weifang with Li Na.
People from different countries compete in kite flying.
Li Na saw many beautiful kites.
Kites were only made of paper.

You look so beautiful!
What kind of clothes are you wearing?
Meimei: Hanfu, a kind of traditional clothing from ancient China.
Oh, Hanfu has such a long history.
Meimei: Yes, about thousands of years.
It has changed greatly across different dynasties.
When do people wear Hanfu now?
Meimei: Teenagers are often seen wearing it at their graduation ceremonies or during holidays.
Some people even wear Hanfu in their daily life.
As a symbol of traditional Chinese culture, Hanfu is getting more and more popular with Chinese people.
I've never worn it.
What a pity!
Meimei: Really?
Hanfu shows are held every year.
Hanfu can be seen everywhere.
Why don't you try it on?
Good idea!
Clothing is a part of culture.
It will help us know more about China.
Meimei: Yes, I'm all for it.
textTranslate:
李娜的假期糟透了。
彼得和李娜一起去潍坊。
来自不同国家的人会进行放风筝比赛。
李娜看到了许多美丽的风筝。
风筝以前只用纸制作。

你看起来真漂亮！
你穿着什么样的衣服？
梅梅：汉服，中国古代的一种传统服装。
哦，汉服有如此悠久的历史。
梅梅：是的，大约有几千年。
汉服在不同朝代发生了巨大的变化。
现在人们什么时候穿汉服？
梅梅：在毕业典礼或节假日期间，经常能看到青少年穿汉服。
有些人甚至在日常生活中穿汉服。
作为中国传统文化的一种象征，汉服越来越受到中国人的喜爱。
我从未穿过汉服。
真遗憾！
梅梅：真的吗？
每年都会举办汉服展。
到处都能看到汉服。
你为什么不试穿一下呢？
好主意！
服饰是文化的一部分。
它将帮助我们更多地了解中国。
梅梅：是的，我非常赞成。

title: Unit 10 · What do symbols tell us?
titleTranslate: 第十单元 · 象征告诉我们什么？
text:
China is the third largest country worldwide, next only to Russia and Canada.
There are 56 ethnic groups in China.
The official language of China is Standard Chinese.
China has rich natural resources, colourful cultural heritage, and diverse customs.

China is an ancient country with great culture and about 5,000 years of history.
The Spring Festival, an ancient festival, also enjoys thousands of years' history.
Today, people still celebrate this traditional festival.
They go back home to get together with their families every year during the festival.

China has lots of famous symbols, such as the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, the Five Great Mountains, pandas, peony, and so on.
The Forbidden City in Beijing was the palace for 24 emperors throughout the Ming and Qing dynasties.
The precious collections in it attract so many tourists.
Pandas are the most popular animal in China.
They are also one of the favourite animals among the Chinese people.
The largest nature park for pandas is in Sichuan Province.
The flower peony is regarded as the symbol of prosperity.
It was much praised by the poets of the Tang Dynasty.

China also has many well-known lakes, such as Qinghai Lake, West Lake, Dongting Lake, and Poyang Lake.
The Qinghai Lake is the largest saltwater lake in China.
Among the rivers in China, the Yangtze River and the Yellow River are quite familiar to Chinese people.
These two great rivers not only are popular, but also have special meanings.
The Yangtze River, also known as the Golden Waterway, is the longest river in China.
The Yellow River is called the Mother River by all Chinese people.

Did you know that tea, the second most popular drink in the world after water, was discovered by accident?
Many people believe that tea was first drunk nearly 5,000 years ago.
It is said that a Chinese chief called Shen Nong first discovered tea as a drink.
One day Shen Nong was boiling water over an open fire.
Some leaves from a tea plant fell into the water and remained there for some time.
It produced a nice smell so he tasted the brown water.
It was quite delicious.
In this way, one of the world's favourite drinks was discovered.

More than 4,000 years later, Lu Yu, "the sage of tea", mentioned Shen Nong in his book Cha Jing.
The book described how tea plants were grown and how to make tea.
It also discussed where the finest tea leaves were produced and what kinds of water were used.

It is believed that tea was brought to Korea and Japan during the 6th and 7th centuries.
In England, tea didn't appear until around 1660, but less than 100 years later, it had become the national drink.
The tea trade from China to Western countries took place in the 19th century.
This helped to spread the popularity of tea and the tea plant to more places around the world.
So next time you have a cup of tea, think about its interesting long history.
textTranslate:
中国是世界上第三大的国家，仅次于俄罗斯和加拿大。
中国有56个民族。
中国的官方语言是普通话。
中国拥有丰富的自然资源、多姿多彩的文化遗产和多样化的风俗习惯。

中国是一个拥有悠久文化、约五千年历史的多民族国家。
春节是一个古老的节日，也已有数千年的历史。
如今，人们仍然庆祝这一传统节日。
每逢节日，人们都会回家与家人团聚。

中国有许多著名的象征，如故宫、长城、五岳、熊猫、牡丹等。
北京故宫是明、清两代二十四位皇帝的宫殿。
其中珍藏的宝物吸引着众多游客。
熊猫是中国最受欢迎的动物。
它们也是中国人民喜爱的动物之一。
世界上最大的熊猫自然保护区位于四川省。
牡丹被视为繁荣昌盛的象征。
它备受唐代诗人的赞美。

中国还有许多著名的湖泊，如青海湖、西湖、洞庭湖和鄱阳湖。
青海湖是中国最大的咸水湖。
在中国的河流中，长江和黄河为中国人民所熟知。
这两条大江大河不仅广为人知，还具有特殊的意义。
长江又称“黄金水道”，是中国最长的河流。
黄河被所有中国人民称为“母亲河”。

你知道吗？茶是世界上仅次于水的第二受欢迎的饮品，而它的发现却是一个意外。
许多人认为，早在近五千年前，人们就开始饮茶了。
据说，一位名叫神农的中国首领最先发现茶可以作为饮品。
一天，神农在露天火堆上烧水。
一些茶树的叶子落进水中，在水里浸泡了一段时间。
水散发出一种香味，于是他尝了尝那棕色的水。
味道非常香甜。
就这样，世界上最受喜爱的饮品之一被发现了。

四千多年后，“茶圣”陆羽在他的著作《茶经》中提到了神农。
这本书描述了茶树如何种植以及如何制茶。
书中还讨论了最优质的茶叶产于何处，以及泡茶可以使用哪些水。

人们认为，茶是在公元六世纪和七世纪传入朝鲜和日本的。
在英国，茶直到约公元1660年才出现，但不到一百年，它便成了国民饮品。
十九世纪，中国与西方国家之间开展了茶叶贸易。
这有助于茶和茶树在世界各地得到更广泛的传播。
所以，下次品茶时，请想想它那悠长而有趣的历史。

title: Unit 10 · Lovely Grandpa Yuan Longping
titleTranslate: 第十单元·可爱的袁隆平爷爷
text:
Yuan Longping was born on 7 September 1930, in Beijing.
He is widely recognized as one of the most well-known agricultural scientists.
From an early age, he was a hard-working student and often asked questions.
Although his parents wanted him to have a job in medicine, Yuan Longping chose to study agriculture in Southwest Agriculture College in Chongqing.
After graduating in 1953, he became a teacher.
It was not until the 1960s that he shifted his focus to researching and improving rice production.

Yuan Longping worked in rice fields for many years, driven by his dream of ensuring that every Chinese person had enough rice to fill their bowls.
However, his contributions went far beyond this aspiration.
He overcame a lot of difficulties and developed the first hybrid rice variety in 1974.
Over the next 50 years, Yuan Longping and his team continued their research, achieving a series of remarkable successes.

In addition, Yuan Longping and his team shared their knowledge with about 14,000 students from nearly 80 countries.
His influence extended not only to China's agricultural development but also to global food security.
He is remembered as a kind, strict, and diligent elderly figure.
Sadly, our lovely grandpa passed away on 22 May 2021, at the age of 91.
Although we lost the "Father of Hybrid Rice", his scientific spirit will last forever.
textTranslate:
袁隆平于1930年9月7日出生在北京。
他被公认为世界上最知名的农业科学家之一。
从小，他就勤奋好学，经常提出问题。
尽管父母希望他从事医学工作，袁隆平仍选择在重庆的西南农业大学学习农业。
1953年毕业后，他成为一名教师。
直到20世纪60年代，他才将重心转向研究和改进水稻生产。

袁隆平在稻田里耕耘多年，秉持着一个梦想：让每个中国人都能吃上足够的米饭。
然而，他的贡献远不止于此。
他克服重重困难，于1974年培育出第一个杂交水稻品种。
此后50年间，袁隆平和他的团队持续开展研究，取得了一系列卓越成就。

此外，袁隆平和他的团队还向来自近80个国家的约14000名学生传授专业知识。
他的影响不仅体现在中国农业发展方面，也体现在保障全球粮食安全方面。
他被人们亲切地记作一位和蔼、严谨而勤勉的长者。
令人 sadly的是，我们可爱的爷爷于2021年5月22日去世，享年91岁。
虽然我们失去了杂交水稻之父，但他的科学精神将永存。

title: Unit 11 · What do you want to say upon graduation?
titleTranslate: 第十一单元·毕业时，你想说些什么？
text:
Good morning, students, teachers, and guests.
Welcome to our junior high graduation ceremony!
To begin with, I would like to congratulate all the new graduates.
You have worked a long time for this moment.
I remember meeting you when you first came here, full of energy and curiosity.
Today, I'm full of pride as I see a room filled with talented youths, full of hope for the future.

As you set out on your life's new journey, first, I would like to say, find your passion, and follow your dreams!
Find what you really love, and put all your energy and effort into it.
Turn your eyes to the stars and keep your feet on the ground.

Second, never give up!
After graduation, everybody will be entering different schools.
No matter where you go, you will face new challenges.
See every challenge as an opportunity: an opportunity to grow, to learn, and to succeed.
So be brave and deal with your challenges through hard work.
Always bear this in mind: Diligence leads to success in one's life.
Hard work will not fail you.

Third, learn to be thankful.
While you have worked hard to finish junior high school, you did not work alone.
Many others have lent hands to help you, and they have worked equally hard to get you to this moment.
These people—your parents, teachers, and friends—have helped make you who you are today.
Always be thankful for their help.
Cherish their love and care forever.
Always remember who you are and where you came from.

Last but not least, the end of junior high is also the beginning of a new life.
Give it your best shot, and have no regrets.
I wish you all success, and I hope we will meet again one day!

Junior high school has been a great journey for me.
I have learnt many things and gained not just knowledge and skills, but also friendship.
The club activities have made my school life richer—many of you know how much I love our drama club!
I will always treasure the unforgettable memories of my time here.
And now, as hard as it is, it's time to say goodbye.

To our teachers, a big "Thank you!" for your hard work, guidance, patience, and support.
To our parents and friends, I want to thank you from the bottom of my heart for your love and support.
Together, we have gone through many ups and downs.
All these experiences have helped us grow and prepared us for new challenges ahead.

Finally, to all my fellow graduating students, "Congratulations!"
Just as our head teacher said at our graduation ceremony, let's follow our passions and keep working hard.
Though our dreams may seem far away, they are worth fighting for.

A class yearbook is usually a book of photos and memories that students create at the end of the school year to remember their time at school.
textTranslate:
同学们、老师们、各位来宾，大家上午好。
欢迎参加我们的初中毕业典礼！
首先，我想祝贺在座的每一位毕业生。
为了这一刻，你们付出了长期的努力。
我还记得你们刚来学校时的样子，满怀活力与好奇。
如今，看到这里坐满了才华横溢、对未来充满希望的青年，我深感自豪。

在踏上人生新征程之际，首先，我想说：找到自己的热爱，追逐自己的梦想！
找到真正喜欢的事物，并为它付出全部精力与努力。
仰望星空，脚踏实地。

其次，永不言弃！
毕业后，每个人都将进入不同的学校。
无论走到哪里，你们都会遇到新的挑战。
要把每一次挑战都看作机会——成长、学习和成功的机会。
因此，要勇敢面对挑战，以勤奋努力迎接挑战。
永远牢记：勤奋是人生成功的关键。
努力不会辜负你。

第三，要懂得感恩。
你们为完成初中学业付出了辛勤努力，但这一路并非独自前行。
许多人为你们伸出援手，他们同样付出了努力，帮助你们走到今天。
这些人——你们的父母、老师和朋友们——帮助你们成长为今天的自己。
要始终感谢他们的帮助。
要永远珍藏他们的爱与关怀。
要始终记住自己是谁，也要记住自己从哪里来。

最后但同样重要的是，初中的结束也是新生活的开始。
全力以赴，不留遗憾。
祝愿大家一切成功，希望我们有一天还能重逢！

初中生活对我而言是一段美好的旅程。
我学到了许多东西，不仅收获了知识与技能，也收获了友谊。
社团活动让我的校园生活更加丰富——你们很多人都知道，我有多么热爱我们的戏剧社团！
我将永远珍藏在这里度过的难忘回忆。
现在，尽管很是不舍，我们还是该说再见了。

衷心感谢老师们的辛勤付出、悉心指导、耐心教诲和大力支持。
衷心感谢父母和朋友们的关爱与支持。
我们一起经历了许多起伏与坎坷。
所有的这些经历都帮助我们成长，并让我们做好迎接未来挑战的准备。

最后，祝所有即将毕业的同学“毕业快乐！”
正如班主任在毕业典礼上所说，让我们追随梦想，继续努力。
尽管梦想看似遥远，但值得我们去拼搏争取。

班级年鉴通常是学生在学年结束时制作的一本照片与回忆集，用来记录他们在学校的时光。

title: Unit 11 · Gui Haichao: A Dream Chaser
titleTranslate: 第11单元 · 桂海潮：逐梦者
text:
Gui Haichao, a fan of space exploration for many years, made his dream of travelling to space come true through his own efforts.
In 1986, Gui Haichao was born in a small village in Yunnan Province.
In 2003, he was excited and attracted by spacecrafts for the first time when he heard the news of the successful launch of the Shenzhou 5.
In 2005, he went to university in Beijing to study spacecraft design and engineering, taking the first significant step toward his dream.
In 2014, he graduated with a doctoral degree in spacecraft design.
In 2017, he became a university professor and did a lot of scientific research on space.

Chances are always for those who are prepared.
Gui Haichao loves long-distance running, biking, and swimming.
This helped him build a strong body.
In 2018, after rounds of physical checks and professional tests, he was selected as one of the chosen few from about 2,500 competitors for a space station project.
On 30 May 2023, the Long March rocket set off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in Gansu Province.
Gui Haichao, who was only 37 years old, was one of the three crew members on the Shenzhou 16.
He became the first Chinese civilian and scientist in space, and his story has set a good example for all young Chinese dream chasers.
textTranslate:
桂海潮多年来一直热爱航天探索，并通过自己的努力实现了遨游太空的梦想。
1986年，桂海潮出生于云南省的一个小村庄。
2003年，他第一次听到神舟5号成功发射的消息时，便对航天器感到兴奋和着迷。
2005年，他前往北京上大学，学习航天器设计与工程专业，迈出了追逐梦想的第一步。
2014年，他以航天器设计博士学位毕业。
2017年，他成为大学教授，并开展了大量航天科学研究。

机会总是留给有准备的人。
桂海潮喜欢长跑、骑自行车和游泳。
这些运动帮助他锻炼出了强健的体魄。
2018年，经过多轮体检和专项测试，他从约2500名竞争者中脱颖而出，成为空间站项目的少数入选者之一。
2023年5月30日，长征系列火箭从甘肃省酒泉卫星发射中心点火升空。
年仅37岁的桂海潮是神舟16号三名航天员之一。
他成为首位进入太空的中国公民和科学家，他的故事为所有中国青年逐梦者树立了榜样。

title: Unit 1 · Young Inventors
titleTranslate: 第1单元 · 少年发明家
text:
You may think that all inventors are adults with rich experience and university degrees, but you would be wrong.
In fact, many famous inventions have been created by teenagers just like you.

At the age of three, Louis Braille became blind as a result of an accident.
At a school for the blind, he was taught to read using books with raised letters.
Blind people would run their fingers over the letters and guess their shapes.
However, sometimes it was confusing because letters like "Q" and "O" were very similar, and they also took up too much space on a page.
To solve these problems, a system was invented where letters were replaced with a code of raised dots.
However, this new method was still too slow and difficult.
At the age of 15, Braille made important improvements to the raised dot system.
He made the code simpler and reduced the number of raised dots.
Braille's system was incredibly successful and is still used today around the world.

Philo Farnsworth was a teenager when he read about the problem of creating an electronic television in a science magazine and became interested in it.
One day, while he was working on a farm, he noticed the straight rows of crops, and it gave him an idea.
Perhaps an image could be broken down into lines, changed into electronic signals, and then sent through the airwaves.
For years, Farnsworth worked to develop his idea, but he faced many challenges along the way.
Many people did not believe his idea would work, and he found it difficult to get money to pay for his research.
However, he never gave up.
When he was 21, he eventually succeeded in sending a simple image using his invention.
This breakthrough was an important step in creating the modern televisions that we use for entertainment today.

These stories show that with a passion for solving problems, anyone can make a difference in the world, no matter how old they are.
So, if you have an idea that you believe in, do not be afraid to go for it.
Who knows?
You may just be the next Louis Braille or Philo Farnsworth.
textTranslate:
你可能以为所有发明家都是拥有丰富经验和大学学位的成年人，但事实并非如此。
事实上，许多著名的发明都是像你们一样的青少年创造出来的。

三岁时，路易·布莱叶因一场事故失明。
在一所盲人学校里，他开始学习阅读盲文书籍。
盲人用手指触摸字母，辨认字母的形状。
然而，有时这种方式会让人感到困惑，因为“Q”和“O”等字母非常相似，而且在一页纸上占据的空间也太大。
为了解决这些问题，人们发明了一种用凸点编码代替字母的系统。
然而，这种新方法仍然过于缓慢和复杂。
15岁时，布莱叶对凸点系统进行了重要改进。
他简化了编码，并减少了凸点的数量。
布莱叶系统取得了极大的成功，如今仍在世界各地使用。

菲尔诺·法恩斯沃思在少年时期读到一篇介绍电子电视研制难题的科学杂志文章，并对这一课题产生了兴趣。
一天，他在农场劳动时注意到作物排列成整齐的直线，由此得到一个启发。
也许可以把图像分解成线条，将其转换为电子信号，再通过电波传送出去。
多年来，法恩斯沃思努力研究如何实现自己的设想，但一路上遇到了许多挑战。
许多人都不相信他的设想能够实现，而且他很难筹到研究经费。
然而，他从未放弃。
21岁时，他终于利用自己的发明成功发送了一幅简单的图像。
这一突破成为制造我们今天用于娱乐的现代电视的重要一步。

这些故事表明，只要热爱解决问题，无论年龄大小，任何人都能在世界上有所作为。
因此，如果你相信自己的设想，就不要害怕去实现它。
谁知道呢？
你或许就是下一个路易·布莱叶或菲洛·法恩斯沃思。

title: Unit 2 · All About Satellites
titleTranslate: 第二单元 · 卫星知识
text:
In October 1957, people listening to radios around the world heard something no one had ever heard before.
For three weeks, there was just "beep, beep, beep".
About one beep a second.
Millions of people sat round their radios just listening for this beep.
The beep itself was not all that amazing.
The amazing thing was the place where it came from—space.
The beep came from the world's first man-made satellite, Sputnik 1.
Sputnik 1 was launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October, 1957.
It was round, made of metal, and more than twice as wide as a basketball.
It weighed about 84 kilograms, travelled at 29,000 kilometres an hour, and took 96.2 minutes to circle Earth.
Sputnik 1 stopped beeping when its radio battery died on 26 October, and it burnt up when it fell back to Earth on 4 January, 1958.
The launch of Sputnik 1 also began the age of satellites.
The first satellites were used for research.
Through them, we can better understand the world we live in.
They also send back photographs that help us to make better maps of our world.
Communication satellites were also soon developed.
These allow TV and radio signals to be sent across oceans or to places thousands of kilometres away.
This is how people can watch TV across continents and oceans.
Weather satellites soon followed.
These can tell us when a storm is coming or whether it will snow next week.
One new kind of satellite that is now becoming more useful to the public is the positioning satellite.
This satellite works with a highly complicated system, like the BDS (BeiDou Navigation Satellite System), which can tell us where our car or even our mobile phone is.
It seems that there is no end to the possible uses of satellites.
The only real limit to their use is our own imagination.
textTranslate:
1957年10月世界各地收听广播的人都听到了一种前所未有的声音。
整整三个星期，广播里只有“哔、哔、哔”的声音。
大约每秒响一声。
数百万人围坐在收音机旁，只为聆听这声“哔”。
哔声本身并没有那么神奇。
神奇的是它来自的地方——太空。
哔声来自世界上第一颗人造卫星——斯普特尼克1号。
斯普特尼克1号由苏联于1957年10月4日发射。
它呈球形，由金属制成，宽度超过篮球的两倍。
它重约84千克，以每小时29,000千米的速度飞行，绕地球一周需要96.2分钟。
1958年1月4日，斯普特尼克1号返回地球并在大气中烧毁；此前在10月26日，其无线电电池耗尽，哔声停止。
斯普特尼克1号的发射也开启了卫星时代。
最初的卫星用于科学研究。
通过这些卫星，我们能够更好地了解我们生活的世界。
它们还会传回照片，帮助我们绘制更准确的世界地图。
通信卫星也很快研制出来了。
它们使电视和广播信号能够跨越海洋，或传送到数千千米之外的地方。
人们正是通过通信卫星，才得以跨越大陆和海洋观看电视。
气象卫星也紧随其后发射升空。
它们能告诉我们风暴何时到来，以及下周是否会降雪。
目前正日益为公众带来便利的一种新型卫星是定位卫星。
定位卫星与高度复杂的系统协同工作，例如北斗卫星导航系统（BDS），后者可以告诉我们汽车甚至手机所在的位置。
卫星的用途似乎没有尽头。
卫星利用方面唯一真正的限制，就是我们自己的想象力。

title: Unit 3 · The Beauty of Chinese Music
titleTranslate: 第三单元 · 中国音乐之美
text:
Last night, one of my Chinese friends took me to a traditional Chinese music concert.
I have always wanted to see traditional Chinese music performed live.
The most common Chinese instruments that I recognized were the erhu, pipa, guzheng, and dizi.
The concert was a superb performance by Chinese artists, attended by both the elderly and the young.
As a foreign audience member, I felt the legacy and continuation of traditional Chinese music in China, and I deeply felt the charm of traditional Chinese music.
The first song that was performed was a familiar tune, "Molihua" ("Jasmine Flower").
It was one of the first Chinese folk songs to become popular outside of China.
The romantic song, played in a simple five-note scale that is characteristic of Chinese music, expressed the love for natural beauty.
It was adapted into the Italian opera Turandot by Puccini.
It was also played during the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games, the opening ceremony of the 2010 Shanghai Expo, and the opening ceremony of the Youth Olympics in Nanjing in 2014.
No wonder it sounded so familiar!
My favourite performance was the erhu solo of "Erquan Yingyue".
The piece has a poetic name, which means "Moon Reflected on Second Spring".
The gifted performer was so expressive that I almost cried along with it as I listened.
The piece is considered one of the masterpieces of Chinese string music and the most famous piece by Chinese musician Abing.
Its sad beauty reminded me of the hardships in Abing's life, but under the sadness, I sensed the musician's optimism and deep love for life.
The concert ended with "Chunjie Xuqu" (the "Spring Festival Overture"), the first movement of the Spring Festival Suite by Li Huanzhi.
Composed in the 1950s, the piece was based on the folk music of northern Shaanxi.
It depicts the Spring Festival celebrated in this region in China during the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression.
The piece had a lively beginning, and then slowed down to a soothing tune.
As the melody played, I felt as though I was among the crowd celebrating the Spring Festival in Shaanxi back then, sharing the people's uplifting spirit and their hopes for a bright future.
textTranslate:
昨晚，一位中国朋友带我去了中国传统音乐会。
我一直想亲眼聆听中国传统音乐的现场演出。
我认出了最常见的中国乐器，有二胡、琵琶、古筝和笛子。
这场音乐会上，中国艺术家进行了精彩表演，现场既有年长观众，也有年轻观众。
作为一个外国观众，我感受到了中国传统音乐在中国的传承与发展，也深深体会到了中国传统音乐的魅力。
第一个演奏的歌曲是大家熟悉的《茉莉花》。
它是最早在中国境外流行起来的中国民歌之一。
这首抒情的歌曲以中国音乐特有的简易五声音阶创作，表达了对自然之美的热爱。
普契尼将这首曲子改编成意大利歌剧《图兰朵》。
它还在2008年北京奥运会、2010年上海世博会开幕式以及2014年南京青奥会开幕式上演奏过。
难怪听起来如此熟悉！
我最喜欢的是《二泉映月》的二胡独奏。
这首曲子的名字富有诗意，意思是“二泉映月”。
这位才华横溢的演奏者情感充沛，我聆听时几乎随着乐曲落泪。
这首曲子被誉为中国弦乐音乐的杰作之一，也是中国音乐家阿炳最著名的作品。
曲中忧伤的美丽使我想起阿炳人生中的坎坷，但在这忧伤之中，我感受到这位音乐家乐观的精神和对生活的深厚热爱。
音乐会以李焕之的《春节序曲》（《春节组曲》的第一乐章）结束。
这首乐曲创作于20世纪50年代，以陕北民间音乐为基础。
它描绘了中国抗日战争时期，陕北地区人民庆祝春节的热闹景象。
乐曲开头活泼热烈，随后逐渐放慢，变为舒缓的旋律。
随着乐曲响起，我仿佛置身于当年陕北人民欢度春节的热闹人群中，分享着他们昂扬的精神和对光明未来的希望。

title: Unit 4 · The Paralympics—Strength and Spirit
titleTranslate: 第四单元·残奥会——力量与精神
text:
Every two years, millions of people from around the world turn on their TVs to watch the Summer or Winter Olympic Games.
However, did you know that a few weeks later, the same city hosts another major sports event—the Paralympic Games?

The Paralympics is an international sports event for athletes with physical disabilities.
The original idea came from a doctor named Ludwig Guttmann in England shortly after World War II.
Guttmann was interested in improving the lives of soldiers dependent on wheelchairs.
He therefore decided to arrange a sports competition between a small group of patients on the same day as the opening of the 1948 Olympic Games.
This small event slowly grew, and in 1960 it became known as the first Paralympic Games.
It was decided that from then on the Paralympics would be held in the same year and country as the Olympic Games.
Nowadays, the Paralympic Games take place in the same cities as the Olympics and use the same venues a short time later.

At the beginning, the Paralympics were open only to people in wheelchairs.
However, in 1976, athletes with visual and other physical disabilities were included.
Generally, athletes at the Paralympics only compete against others with the same kind of disability.

The Paralympics' goal has always been to help those with disabilities to improve their physical health and bring them joy and purpose.
The motto for the Olympic movement is "Faster, Higher, Stronger—Together".
The Paralympic Games follow this motto, showing the amazing strength and spirit of athletes with physical disabilities.
textTranslate:
每隔两年，数以百万计的来自世界各地的人都会打开电视，观看夏季或冬季奥运会。
然而，你知道吗？几周之后，同一座城市还会举办另一项重大体育赛事——残奥会。

残奥会是一项面向身体残疾运动员的国际体育赛事。
这一构想最初来自英格兰一位名叫路德维希·古特曼的医生，时间是在第二次世界大战结束后不久。
古特曼致力于改善轮椅士兵的生活。
因此，他决定在1948年奥运会开幕当天，安排一小群患者举行体育比赛。
这项小型活动逐渐发展起来，并于1960年成为首届残奥会。
当时决定，从此以后，残奥会与奥运会在同一年度、同一国家举行。
如今，残奥会与奥运会先后在同一座城市举行，并使用相同的比赛场馆。

最初，残奥会只对轮椅使用者开放。
然而，1976年，视力残疾及其他身体残疾的运动员也被纳入其中。
一般来说，残奥会运动员只与患有同类残疾的运动员比赛。

残奥会始终旨在帮助残障人士增强体质，给他们带来快乐和人生价值。
奥林匹克运动的格言是“更快、更高、更强——更团结”。
残奥会遵循这一格言，展现身体残疾运动员非凡的力量与精神。

title: Unit 5 · The 24 Solar Terms
titleTranslate: 第五单元·二十四节气
text:
More than 2,000 years ago, the ancient Chinese developed the 24 solar terms—a unique "calendar" to understand nature.
They divided the year into 24 periods, each lasting 15 or 16 days.
These terms were a guide for farmers—informing them of when to carry out certain farming activities.
Many traditional Chinese festivals and folk customs are also related to the 24 solar terms.

The year begins with lichun (Start of Spring).
Among the many traditions for welcoming spring is a popular custom, "biting the spring", where people eat spring pancakes or spring rolls.
As the temperature rises and rainfall increases, nature slowly awakens.
Farmers prepare their fields so that they can plant their crops during guyu (Grain Rain), the last term of the season.

Lixia (Start of Summer) marks the transition from spring to summer.
Summer is a busy time for farmers.
During the third solar term of summer, mangzhong (Grain of Ear), farmers in northern China harvest winter wheat, while farmers in southern China are busy planting summer rice.
"Ear"here means the top part of a grain plant, such as wheat, that contains the seeds.
It is no wonder mangzhong sounds like "busy with planting" in Chinese!

Liqiu (Start of Autumn) marks the coming of a harvesting season.
There is a saying that goes, "If it rains on the day of Start of Autumn, a good harvest is expected."
By the day of qiufen (the Autumn Equinox), the middle point of autumn, the weather in most areas becomes cool and leaves change in colour from green to orange and yellow.
The Mid-Autumn Festival, a festival full of poetry and imagination, is celebrated around this time.
Families and friends gather to admire the full moon and eat mooncakes.

Winter is a time for farmers to store their harvests and rest.
After lidong (Start of Winter), the weather gradually changes from cool to cold.
A traditional custom on the day of Start of Winter is to eat dumplings.
The delicious and nutritious dumplings embody a warm wish for a cozy winter.
Dahan (Major Cold) is the final term of the year and the coldest time of the year.
As the new year draws near, families start to prepare for the Spring Festival.

Today, the 24 solar terms still play an important role in life.
They remind us of how nature changes through the year and reflect the Chinese wisdom of living in harmony with nature.
textTranslate:
两千多年前，中国古人创立了二十四节气——这是一种认识自然的独特“历法”。
古人将一年分为二十四个时段，每个时段持续15天或16天。
节气是指导农民劳作的依据——告诉他们何时进行某些农事活动。
许多中国传统节日和民俗也与二十四节气有关。

一年从立春开始。
迎春的传统习俗之一是盛行的“咬春”，即人们吃春饼或春卷。
随着气温回升、降雨增多，大自然渐渐苏醒。
农民整好田地，以便在谷雨这个季节最后一个节气里播种庄稼。

立夏标志着春天向夏天的过渡。
夏季是农民忙碌的季节。
在夏季的第三个节气芒种，中国北方的农民收获冬小麦，而中国南方的农民正忙于种植夏稻。
这里的“芒”指麦子等谷类植物顶端结有种子的部分。
难怪“芒种”在汉语中听起来像“忙于种植”。

立秋标志着收获季节的来临。
有一种说法：“立秋逢雨，万物丰收。”
到了秋分这一天，也就是秋季的中点，大多数地区的天气开始转凉，树叶由绿色变成橙色和黄色。
充满诗意和想象力的中秋节，大多在这个时候庆祝。
家人们和朋友们聚在一起赏月，吃月饼。

冬季是农民储藏收获物和休养生息的时节。
立冬之后，天气逐渐由凉爽转为寒冷。
立冬当天吃饺子是一项传统习俗。
美味又营养的饺子寄托着人们对温暖舒适冬天的美好祝愿。
大寒是一年中的最后一个节气，也是一年中最寒冷的时节。
随着新年临近，家家户户开始筹备春节。

如今，二十四节气仍在人们的生活中发挥着重要作用。
它们提醒我们大自然如何随四季变化，也体现了中国人与自然和谐共处的智慧。

title: Unit 6 · Into the Unknown
titleTranslate: 第6单元·走向未知
text:
A lost city under the sea in the Atlantic Ocean.
Gardens up in the air in an ancient city in the Middle East.
These are just two famous examples of historical mysteries that have fascinated people for thousands of years.
Why are people so interested in such things?
Well, humans are naturally curious.
We like to use our imagination.
Even when reading, many people love to read about places and times that might not be possible to visit in real life.
Also, we like to find explanations for the things we do not fully understand.
Sometimes we may just want answers to the simple questions of where and why.

Around 360 BCE, the ancient Greek writer Plato told the story of Atlantis, an island in the Atlantic Ocean.
The founders of the island were half god and half human, and they were very rich and powerful.
However, when they became too greedy and wicked, the gods made a terrible night of fire and earthquakes, and the island sank into the sea.

Although it is probably just a legend, later European writers believed it could be true.
There were many arguments as archaeologists tried to identify the actual location of the island.
"Pick a spot on the map, and someone has said that Atlantis was there," said a professor at the New York State Museum.
Some thought it could be in the Mediterranean Sea, while others said it might be off the coast of Spain.
Yet another idea was that Atlantis could be Antarctica.
But was the island real?
We may never know.

Another famous mystery involves a wonderful collection of gardens in the ancient city of Babylon, south of today's Baghdad, the capital of Iraq.
The Hanging Gardens of Babylon is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Many writers described these gardens as having beautiful plants and flowers hanging from the walls of the city.
However, unlike the other wonders, scientists today argue about whether these gardens ever existed at all.
A researcher from Oxford University claimed that there were such gardens, but they could have been in a completely different city, Nineveh, which was near the modern city of Mosul, in northern Iraq.
Unfortunately, both sites suffered damage from wars, so it may be difficult for archaeologists ever to solve this mystery.
textTranslate:
大西洋海底一座失落的城市。
中东一座古城中悬于空中的花园。
这只是两个历史谜团的著名例子，它们吸引着人们长达数千年。
为什么人们对这类事物如此感兴趣？
因为人类天生充满好奇。
我们喜欢发挥自己的想象力。
即使在阅读时，许多人也喜欢阅读那些现实中可能无法到访的地方和时代。
此外，我们还喜欢为那些尚未完全理解的事物寻找解释。
有时，我们只是想得到“在哪里”和“为什么”这些简单问题的答案。

约公元前360年，古希腊作家柏拉图讲述了亚特兰蒂斯的故事。那是大西洋中的一座岛屿。
岛屿的创建者半人半神，而且十分富有和强大。
然而，当他们变得过于贪婪和邪恶时，诸神降下一个可怕的夜晚，火焰与地震接踵而至，岛屿沉入海中。

尽管这很可能只是一个传说，但后来的欧洲作家相信它或许真实存在。
考古学家试图确定这座岛屿的实际位置，因而产生了许多争论。
纽约州立博物馆的一位教授说：“在地图上随便指一个地方，就有人说亚特兰蒂斯曾在那里。”
有人认为它可能位于地中海，也有人说它也许在西班牙近海。
还有一种观点认为亚特兰蒂斯可能就是南极洲。
但这座岛屿真的存在过吗？
我们也许永远无法知道。

另一个著名谜团与巴比伦古城中的一组奇妙花园有关。巴比伦位于今天伊拉克首都巴格达以南。
巴比伦空中花园是古代世界七大奇迹之一。
许多作家描述过这些花园，说城墙上悬挂着美丽的植物和花卉。
然而，与其他奇迹不同，如今的科学家对空中花园是否真的存在存在争议。
牛津大学的一名研究员声称，这些花园确实存在，但它们可能位于另一座城市尼尼微。尼尼微位于今天伊拉克北部的摩苏尔附近。
遗憾的是，这两个地点都遭受了战争的破坏，因此考古学家可能很难解开这个谜团。

title: Unit 7 · Rodin and Balzac
titleTranslate: 第七单元 · 罗丹与巴尔扎克
text:
One of the most famous modern sculptors is Auguste Rodin (1840–1917).
Rodin was born in Paris, and he trained to be a sculptor from an early age.
For many years, he had to make a living by decorating buildings.

Things changed for Rodin in 1875 when he had a chance to visit Italy.
He found new inspiration when he saw the works of Michelangelo.
His breakthrough work—The Age of Bronze—was completed that same year.
It was so realistic that people thought he had just made a cast of a human body.
When Rodin proved that it was truly his work, he became the talk of the town.

While The Thinker is Rodin's most famous sculpture, his sculpture of Balzac is also influential.
Honoré de Balzac (1799–1850) was one of France's most beloved writers.
After his death, it was decided in 1891 that a statue should be created in his honour.
Rodin was supposed to complete the statue in 18 months, but in the end it took seven years!
To make things worse, at first it was rejected by the public because people did not think it looked like Balzac at all.
Rodin's reply was that the statue was not supposed to look like Balzac's body—it was supposed to show Balzac's character and spirit.
Upset about the rejection, Rodin took the sculpture home and refused to show it again.
It was not until 1939 that the first bronze version of the sculpture was created and put on display.

Today, the sculpture, Balzac, is celebrated as one of the first truly modern sculptures and as one of the greatest sculptures ever made.
The importance of this work and others is that Rodin was able to break away from traditional Greek and Roman style sculptures and create something entirely new.
Rodin's sculptures are full of emotion and life, and they speak to modern audiences in a way that traditional sculptures do not.
This is why Rodin is still celebrated and studied by artists today.
textTranslate:
奥古斯特·罗丹（1840—1917）是现代最著名的雕塑家之一。
罗丹出生在巴黎，从小就接受了雕塑训练。
多年来，他不得不靠装饰建筑物维持生计。

1875年，罗丹有机会访问意大利，他的生活从此发生了变化。
看到米开朗琪罗的作品后，他获得了新的灵感。
他的突破性作品《青铜时代》也在同年完成。
这部作品非常逼真，以至于人们认为他只是制作了一具人体的铸模。
当罗丹证明这确实是自己的作品后，他成了全城谈论的人物。

虽然《思想者》是罗丹最著名的雕塑，但他的巴尔扎克雕像也颇具影响力。
奥诺雷·德·巴尔扎克（1799—1850）是法国最受爱戴的作家之一。
他去世后，人们决定于1891年为他建造一座雕像，以表达对他的敬意。
罗丹原应在18个月内完成这座雕像，但最终却花了七年！
更糟的是，这座雕像起初遭到公众拒绝，因为人们认为它一点也不像巴尔扎克。
罗丹回应说，这座雕像本来就不该表现巴尔扎克的外貌，而应该表现他的性格和精神。
罗丹对这一拒绝非常不满，于是把雕像带回家，并拒绝再次公开展示。
直到1939年，这座雕塑的第一个青铜版本才被制作出来并公开展出。

如今，这座名为《巴尔扎克》的雕塑被誉为最早的真正现代雕塑作品之一，也是有史以来最伟大的雕塑之一。
这部作品及其他作品的重要意义在于，罗丹能够摆脱传统的希腊和罗马雕塑风格，创造出全新的艺术形式。
罗丹的雕塑充满情感和生命力，它们以一种传统雕塑无法做到的方式与现代观众产生共鸣。
因此，直到今天，罗丹仍受到人们的颂扬，也一直是艺术家研究和学习的对象。

title: Unit 8 · The Problem with Plastic
titleTranslate: 第八单元 · 塑料带来的问题
text:
Plastic is one of the most useful materials in the world.
It provides many benefits to our lives because it is cheap and convenient.
For example, two or three hundred years ago, clothes were quite expensive, so many people only had one or two sets of clothes to wear.
Now, with plastics like nylon and polyester, clothes have become much cheaper.
Plastic can also be used to replace other things that are rare or valuable.
For example, things like piano keys, which were once made from ivory, are now usually made from plastic.
This saved the lives of many elephants.

However, while plastic has many benefits, it also causes lots of problems.
Some plastic is so strong that it takes more than 400 years to break down before returning safely to the environment.
When plastic is put in a landfill, the harmful materials inside can get into the soil and water underground.
When plastic rubbish is burnt, it fills the air with harmful gas.
Another problem is that plastic rubbish is often thrown on the ground.
Rain washes that rubbish into the rivers.
From there, it is swept out to the sea.
Sea animals can get caught in it or hurt by it.
Worse yet, sometimes fish eat the plastic as food, and it gets into their bodies.
When the fish get to our dining table, the plastic could get into humans' bodies and harm our health.

What can we do about these problems?
The best solution, for now, is to use less plastic.
For example, bring your own reusable bag when shopping.
Buy products, such as clothing and toothbrushes, made of natural materials.
Avoid buying products with plastic packaging.
Say no to single-use plastic items—plastic spoons and forks, plastic food containers and straws, etc.

While plastic is convenient and useful, in the end, most of it will last longer on our planet than we will.
Let us not leave this problem to our future generations when we can deal with it now.
textTranslate:
塑料是世界上最有用的材料之一。
塑料价格低廉，使用方便，因此为我们的生活带来了许多好处。
例如，两三百年前，衣服相当昂贵，因此许多人只有一两套衣服可穿。
如今，有了尼龙和聚酯等塑料制品，衣服便宜多了。
塑料还可用于替代其他稀有或昂贵的东西。
例如，琴键过去曾用象牙制作，如今通常由塑料制成。
这拯救了许多大象的生命。

然而，塑料虽然有许多好处，也会造成许多问题。
有些塑料非常坚固，需要400多年才能降解，安全地回归环境。
塑料被填入垃圾填埋场后，其中的有害物质会渗入地下土壤和水体。
塑料垃圾被焚烧时，会使空气中充满有害气体。
另一个问题是，塑料垃圾经常被扔在地上。
雨水会把这些垃圾冲入河流。
随后，它们会被冲入大海。
海洋动物可能被垃圾缠住或受到伤害。
更糟糕的是，有时鱼会把塑料当作食物吃掉，塑料就会进入它们体内。
当这些鱼被端上我们的餐桌时，塑料可能会进入人体，危害我们的健康。

对于这些问题，我们能做些什么呢？
目前最好的解决办法是少使用塑料。
例如，购物时自带可重复使用的购物袋。
购买由天然材料制成的产品，如衣服和牙刷。
避免购买带有塑料包装的产品。
拒绝使用一次性塑料制品——塑料勺和叉、塑料食品容器和吸管等。

塑料虽然方便实用，但归根结底，大多数塑料在地球上存在的时间都会比我们更久。
现在我们就能解决这个问题，不要把它留给我们的子孙后代。

title: Unit 9 · The Sydney Opera House
titleTranslate: 第九单元 · 悉尼歌剧院
text:
The Sydney Opera House is one of the most famous buildings in the world.
It is Sydney's best-known landmark and an international symbol.
The Sydney Opera House is as representative of Australia as the Pyramids are of Egypt.
The Opera House with a "sailing roof" was designed by the famous Danish architect, Jørn Utzon.
The base for the building was started in 1959.
Utzon spent four years designing the Opera House.
In 1963, the designs were finished and the second stage of construction began.
In 1967, the inside was decorated.
It took 14 years in total to build the Opera House.
In 1973, the Opera House was officially put into use.

The Sydney Opera House cost around 100 million dollars, which was funded by the public.
It is about 183 metres long and 120 metres wide.
The roof of the building consists of more than 2,000 panels.
Each year, this fantastic building attracts over 200,000 tourists to visit or enjoy events in it.

The Opera House reaches out into the harbour.
When seen from the air or a ferry, the skyline of the Sydney Opera House, the blue water of the harbour, and the Sydney Harbour Bridge are so beautiful, amazing, and unforgettable.
textTranslate:
悉尼歌剧院是世界上最著名的建筑之一。
它是悉尼最著名的地标，也是一张国际名片。
悉尼歌剧院之于澳大利亚，正如金字塔之于埃及。
这座拥有“帆形屋顶”的歌剧院由著名的丹麦建筑师约恩·乌松设计。
建筑的地基于1959年开始动工。
乌松花了四年时间设计歌剧院。
1963年，设计完成，第二阶段建设开始。
1967年，内部装饰完成。
歌剧院总共建了14年。
1973年，悉尼歌剧院正式投入使用。

悉尼歌剧院耗资约1亿美元，由公共资金提供。
它长约183米，宽约120米。
建筑的屋顶由2,000多块预制板组成。
这座非凡的建筑每年吸引超过200,000名游客前来参观或参加其中的活动。

歌剧院伸入海湾之中。
从空中或渡轮上望去，悉尼歌剧院的天际线、海港的碧蓝海水以及悉尼海港大桥构成了一幅美丽、震撼而难忘的景象。

title: Unit 10 · Beijing Opera
titleTranslate: 第十单元 · 京剧
text:
Beijing opera is a traditional form of Chinese drama, and it is the most popular Chinese opera genre.
With a history of approximately 200 years, it developed from various other drama forms, primarily from "Anhui opera" which was popular in southern China during the 18th century.

Over the past centuries, the roles in Beijing opera have evolved and simplified into the four major roles we know today: Sheng, Dan, Jing, and Chou.
The theatrical art form of Beijing opera includes singing, dancing, and spoken dialogue.

One foreign traveller described his initial experience of watching Beijing opera.
He said, "I was somewhat bored at first, but gradually, I became more interested.
Eventually, I was strongly drawn to Beijing opera, even though I knew nothing about the background of the drama."

Today, Beijing opera is considered one of China's cultural treasures and has also spread to other countries.
It acts as a bridge, introducing traditional Chinese culture to other parts of the world.
textTranslate:
京剧是中国戏曲的传统形式，也是中国最受欢迎的戏曲剧种。
京剧约有200年的历史，由多种其他戏剧形式发展而来，其中主要源于18世纪流行于中国南方的“安徽戏曲”。

几百年来，京剧的角色逐渐演变和简化为今天我们所熟知的四大行当：生、旦、净、丑。
京剧这种戏剧艺术形式包括唱、舞和念白。

一位外国旅行者描述了自己第一次观看京剧的经历。
他说：“起初我有些无聊，但渐渐地，我越来越感兴趣。
最终，我被京剧深深吸引住了，尽管我对这出戏的背景一无所知。”

如今，京剧被视为中国文化遗产之一，并且已传播到其他国家。
它架起了一座桥梁，将中国传统文化介绍给世界其他地区。

title: Unit 11 · See It Through
titleTranslate: 第十一单元 · 坚持到底
text:
When you're up against a trouble, If the worst is bound to happen, Meet it squarely, face to face; Spite of all that you can do, Lift your chin and set your shoulders, Running from it will not save you, Plant your feet and take a brace.
See it through!
When it's vain to try to dodge it, Do the best that you can do; Even hope may seem but futile, You may fail, but you may conquer, When with troubles you're beset, See it through!
But remember you are facing Just what other men have met.
Black may be the clouds about you You may fail, but fall still fighting; And your future may seem grim, Don't give up, whate'er you do; But don't let your nerve desert you; Eyes front, head high to the finish.
Keep yourself in fighting trim.
See it through!
textTranslate:
当你遭遇麻烦，纵然最坏的情况注定要发生，也要勇敢面对，正视它；尽管你已经竭尽全力，逃避也不能让你得救，昂首挺胸，站稳脚跟，勇敢迎接挑战。
坚持到底！
明知无法躲避，也要尽力去做；即使希望看似渺茫，你可能失败，却也能获胜。困难缠身，也要坚持到底！
但请记住，你面对的正是其他人也曾面对过的一切。
头顶的乌云或许漆黑一片，你可能失败，却要继续战斗；未来或许看似 bleak，不要放弃，无论如何；不要丧失勇气；挺胸向前，坚持到底。
保持战斗状态。
坚持到底！

title: Unit 11 · It's a Long Way
titleTranslate: 第十一单元·漫漫长路
text:
It's a long way the sea-winds blow Over the sea-plains blue, — But longer far has my heart to go Before its dreams come true.

It's work we must, and love we must, And do the best we may, And take the hope of dreams in trust To keep us day by day.

It's a long way the sea-winds blow— But somewhere lies a shore— Thus down the tide of Time shall flow My dreams forevermore*.

Because of my fur and horns, many people have tried to hunt me before.
That's horrible.
You saved my life and I owe you.
I won't let anyone know about you—I promise!
You are a good man.
I trust you.
Goodbye!
Thank you again, and goodbye! [The deer and the raven exit stage left.
The man exits stage right.]
Where is my servant?
At your service, my king.
Do you know anything about this nine-coloured deer?
No, my king.
Go find this deer right now!
I will give a large reward to whoever finds it.
Yes, my king!

[In the palace.
The king and the queen sit.
The guards and servants stand on the sides.]
Come forward, good man.
Do you really know where that deer is?
If you can get the deer's fur and horns, I will give you the large reward I promised.
Yes, my king.
I will lead you to find that deer. [Scratches his face.]
I'm terribly sorry.
This man didn't keep his promise and did a terrible thing to you who saved his life.
And all I thought about was what my wife wanted.
I am so ashamed of myself.
Will you please forgive me?
You are a fine king.
If you can just promise me one thing, I will forgive you.
I will keep my word.
Please tell me what it is.
I hope your people can live with me in harmony from now on, instead of hunting me all the time.
You have my word.
It's so kind of you.
It's time for me to leave.
May you and your people live a good life.
Goodbye! [Leaves the stage.]
Goodbye!
And thank you for your blessing! [Turns to the man.]
I should have never trusted you.
You betrayed the deer who saved your life.
I'm a sinner.
Have mercy on me, my king!
I now order that no one should harm the nine-coloured deer.
It will be protected and live a happy life unharmed by my people.
And now, let's return to the palace!
Yes, my king!

[At the ballroom in the palace.
It is filled with people dressed in fine clothes and jewellery, talking, laughing, and dancing.]
Thank you so much for bringing me to this ball!
Look at the prince and the minister, and their wives.
They look gorgeous with their dresses and their shiny diamonds.
I'm so happy!
As long as you're happy, my dear.
Come and meet my boss.
Mr Romponneau, this is my wife, Mathilde.
Romponneau: [Walks up to Mathilde and bows.]
Nice to meet you, madame.
Your husband has been such a good help to me at work.
And you look stunning tonight.
May I have this dance?
It's so nice to meet you too, Mr Romponneau.
It's my pleasure.
See you later, Loisel.
Take your time and enjoy yourself.
Look at that fair lady with her shiny diamond necklace.
She looks gorgeous!
Do you recognize her?
No, I have never seen her at any ball.
She must be a newcomer here, with a rich husband.
Let me ask her for the next dance.
Then we'll know more. [Mathilde dances with different people in turn.
Loisel slowly falls asleep on a chair at the side of the room.
After dancing for the whole night, Mathilde walks over to Loisel and wakes him up.] [Mathilde and Loisel look through all the jewellery shops in the city until they find a similar necklace.]
Oh, look at this.
It looks exactly the same as Jeanne's.
We're so [In Loisel and Mathilde's new flat.
It is much smaller and shabbier.
Loisel comes back looking tired and stressed.]
Hi dear, I'm so hungry.
I went to the trade company after work and did the accounting there for three hours without dinner.
I'm so sorry to hear that.
Here's some soup.
I made it with the last of our potatoes.
After the day I've had, even potato soup is a feast for me.
How was your day?
It was just as terrible as every day has been.
I washed all the dishes and clothes with cold water and my bare hands.
I climbed up and down the four floors with buckets of water.
I had the usual quarrel with Mrs Butcher because she wouldn't sell me cheese on credit.
Well, look on the bright side!
Next week, the loan for the necklace will finally be paid off, and we'll be free.
We'll have our lives back again!
But I'm no longer the beautiful young woman I once was.
With all this hard work, I've aged 30 years!
No, my dear.
You're just too tired.
Drink some hot soup and get some rest.
Tomorrow will be another day.
Thank you, my darling, but I can't.
I have to go and do the laundry for that rich family up the hill.
I'll be back late tonight.
I have got two more cases of work.
I didn't finish them last Sunday, so I can't walk with you there.
Sorry.
It doesn't matter.
Give me your thick coat.
It's getting cold outside. [Mathilde finishes her soup and leaves.] [One Sunday morning, Mathilde is walking slowly down a street.
Jeanne walks towards her but does not recognize her.]
Hello, Jeanne.
Oh, madame.
Do I know you?
You must have the wrong person.
It's me, Mathilde.
Mathilde?
Is that you? [Stares closely.]
It really is you!
How long has it been since we met last time?
Ten years.
Ten years?
But look at you!
Your hair is totally grey, and your hands are so rough.
You must have been through a lot.
What happened?
textTranslate:
海风越过蔚蓝的海原，吹了很长很长的路——但在梦想成真之前，我的心要走的路更长。

我们必须工作，也必须去爱，尽我们所能，并满怀希望地信任梦想，让我们日复一日地坚持下去。

海风仍在吹，漫漫长路——但某个地方总有一片海岸——因此，时光的潮汐将永远把我的梦想带向远方*。

因为我的皮毛和角，曾经有许多人试图猎捕我。
那太可怕了。
你救了我的命，我欠你一份恩情。
我不会让任何人知道你的事——我保证！
你是个好人。
我相信你。
再见！
再次感谢你，再见！[鹿和乌鸦从舞台左侧退场。
男人从舞台右侧退场。]
我的仆人在哪里？
为您效劳，我的国王。
你知道这只九色鹿的事吗？
不知道，我的国王。
立刻去找这只鹿！
谁找到它，我就重重赏赐谁。
是，我的国王！

[在宫殿里。
国王和王后坐着。
侍卫和仆人站在两旁。]
过来，好人。
你真的知道那只鹿在哪里吗？
如果你能取得鹿的皮毛和角，我就把答应给你的重赏赐给你。
是，我的国王。
我会带你去寻找那只鹿。[挠了挠脸。]
我非常抱歉。
这个人没有遵守承诺，还伤害了救过他命的你。
而我只顾着考虑我妻子想要什么。
我为自己感到非常羞愧。
你能原谅我吗？
你是一位好国王。
如果你答应我一件事，我就会原谅你。
我会遵守诺言。
请告诉我是什么事。
我希望从今以后，你的臣民能与我和睦相处，而不是时时追猎我。
我向您保证。
您真是太好了。
我该走了。
愿你和你的臣民过上幸福的生活。
再见！［退下舞台。］
再见！
感谢您的祝福！［转身面向那位男士。］
我不该相信你。
你背叛了救过你的那头鹿。
我是个罪人。
饶恕我吧，我的王！
我现在下令，任何人都不得伤害九色鹿。
它将受到保护，在我的臣民的守护下幸福生活，不受伤害。
现在，我们回宫殿去吧！
是，我的国王！

［在宫殿的舞厅里。
厅里挤满了衣着华贵、珠光宝气的人们，他们交谈、欢笑、跳舞。］
非常感谢您带我来参加这场舞会！
看看王子、大臣和他们的妻子们。
她们穿着华丽的礼服，戴着闪亮的钻石，真漂亮。
我太开心了！
只要你快乐，我亲爱的。
来见见我的上司。
罗蒙诺先生，这是我妻子玛蒂尔德。
罗蒙诺：［走到玛蒂尔德面前，鞠躬。］
很高兴认识您，夫人。
您丈夫在工作上帮了我很大的忙。
您今晚真是光彩照人。
我可以邀请您跳一支舞吗？
我也很高兴认识您，罗蒙诺先生。
这是我的荣幸。
一会儿见，洛塞尔。
您慢慢来，尽情享受吧。
看那位佩戴着闪亮钻石项链的美丽女士。
她真漂亮！
您认识她吗？
不，我从没在任何舞会上见过她。
她一定是这里的新面孔，而且有一位富裕的丈夫。
让我请她跳下一支舞。
这样我们就能多了解她一些了。［玛蒂尔德依次与不同的人跳舞。
洛塞尔渐渐在房间角落的一把椅子上睡着了。］
整整跳了一夜舞后，玛蒂尔德走到洛伊塞尔身边，叫醒了他。[玛蒂尔德和洛伊塞尔跑遍城里的所有珠宝店，终于找到一条相似的项链。]
哦，快看这个。
它和珍妮的那条一模一样。
我们真是……[在洛伊塞尔和玛蒂尔德的新公寓里。
这里比原来的房子小得多，也破旧得多。
洛伊塞尔回来时，看上去疲惫不堪，满腹愁绪。]
亲爱的，我饿极了。
下班后，我去商行做了三个小时的账，连晚饭都没吃。
听到你过得这么辛苦，我很难过。
这里有些汤。
这是用我们最后几个土豆做的。
经历了这样的一天，连土豆汤对我来说都是盛宴了。
你今天过得怎么样？
和往常每一天一样糟透了。
所有碗碟和衣服都是我用冷水和双手洗的。
我提着水桶，在四层楼之间上上下下。
我又和巴彻太太照例吵了一架，因为她不肯赊卖给我奶酪。
好了，往好处想吧！
下周，买项链的贷款终于可以还清了，我们就自由了。
我们终于可以过回自己的生活了！
可我已经不再是当年那个美丽的年轻女子了。
这些辛苦的工作让我仿佛一下子老了三十岁！
不，亲爱的。
你只是太累了。
喝点热汤，好好休息吧。
明天又是新的一天。
谢谢你，亲爱的，可我不能休息。
我得去山上那户富人家洗衣服。
我今晚会很晚才回来。
我还有两批活儿没做。
上个星期天我没做完，所以今天不能陪你走了。
对不起。
没关系。
把你的厚外套给我。
外面越来越冷了。[玛蒂尔德喝完汤，离开了。] [一个星期天早晨，玛蒂尔德正沿着街道缓慢地走着。
珍妮朝她走来，却没有认出她。]
你好，珍妮。
哦，夫人。
我认识你吗？
你一定是认错人了。
我是玛蒂尔德。
玛蒂尔德？
是你吗？［仔细端详。］
真的是你！
我们上次见面后有多久了？
十年。
十年？
但看看你！
你的头发全白了，双手也粗糙得很。
你一定经历了很多事情。
发生了什么？
